subject.title: [Feature]:  Non-blocking heartbeat execution to prevent message processing delays

question: Should OpenClaw add a separate heartbeat execution lane or worker model, or continue addressing heartbeat contention through narrower retry, idle, and isolation mitigations?
rationale: The requested change crosses core scheduling, session state, and message delivery ordering, so automation cannot safely choose the permanent execution boundary without maintainer product and architecture intent.

options.title: Design isolated heartbeat execution
options.body: Define and implement a maintained heartbeat execution contract with explicit session, delivery, tool, and live-channel proof requirements before code changes.

options.title: Keep narrow mitigations
options.body: Continue improving retry cadence, idle gating, isolated sessions, and lightweight context without introducing a new execution model.

options.title: Defer until live evidence
options.body: Wait for a live reproduction with current main and clearer latency requirements before changing heartbeat architecture.

recommendation.title: Design isolated heartbeat execution
recommendation.body: Define and implement a maintained heartbeat execution contract with explicit session, delivery, tool, and live-channel proof requirements before code changes.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest current and historical connection to the heartbeat runner, wake scheduling, and docs contract.
